summary: Streaming sessions terminate after header rotation during KV-cache warmup in prod
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports long-running streaming completions disconnecting mid-stream during request flows that trigger KV-cache warmup. Impact: multiple merchant endpoints experience intermittent 5xx/stream resets leading to failed payments and degraded UX. Observed pattern ties failures to requests that include rotating trace headers (X-Trace-Id/X-B3) and large set-cookie/tracing metadata generated by the customer's SDK.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, prod/us-east, routes pinned to gpt-open-13b-v1. Problem began after a rollout of improved tracing middleware in the customer's SDK (they started rotating trace headers per-chunk) and coincided with higher percentage of cold KV-cache misses at the serving layer.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send a streaming generate request against the Redwood hosted endpoint with an initial request producing long KV-cache warmup (cold model + cold KV cache).
2) Have the client rotate/replace tracing headers mid-stream (simulate SDK that sets new X-Trace-Id every 10s).
3) Observe the streamed chunks; after header rotation the connection is terminated with 502/stream-reset and the client sees incomplete completion.
4) Repeat with warmed KV cache and rotating headers disabled — issue does not reproduce reliably.
observed_behavior: Streaming TCP connection reset by ALB/APIGW after header rotation; client receives truncated completion. ALB logs show Backend connection closed with error, idle-timeout metric spikes and 'Request length beyond configured max header size' is NOT consistently present. Upstream serving instances log 'client disconnected during send' and partial token emission.
expected_behavior: Streaming remains stable for duration of completion regardless of header updates sent by client during the same logical session (we should tolerate header changes or negotiate without terminating connection).
logs:
ALB access logs: multiple entries with target_status_code '-' and target_processing_time ~30s prior to disconnect. APIGW proxy logs show sequence: initial HTTP/2 stream open, data frames, then a HEADERS frame with new trace headers, then ALB closes target connection. SRE packet capture indicates HTTP/2 header re-encoding triggered APIGW to re-chunk the upstream request and the ALB idle timer restarted.
Related snippets: 
- alb-20260310-verbose.log: target:172.31.11.22 - - [10/Mar/2026:14:22:10 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" - - - - "-"
- serving-runtime-prod-13b-0 stdout: "kv-cache: miss, starting prefix load; chunk 1 emitted; write error: broken pipe"
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header re-encoding on the API gateway when receiving mid-stream HEADERS frames causes the gateway to buffer and reset the downstream connection rather than stream-through. Correlated factors: (a) KV-cache warmup increases time-to-first-byte for downstream responses, (b) client-side header rotation introduces extra HEADERS frames mid-stream, and (c) ALB idle timeout is at default 60s which interacts poorly when proxy restarts timers on header re-encoding.

What we checked:
- Replayed traffic with header rotation disabled — reproduces less than 5% of the time.
- Increased ALB idle timeout to 120s on a test target group — reproduces less and connections survive longer.
- Packet captures show client continues to send frames but ALB tears down the target connection after a header frame.
- Verified headers do not exceed max header size limit.

Working hypothesis: APIGW treats mid-stream header frames as a change that triggers buffer flush/rewrite path that restarts idle timers and sometimes causes premature target disconnect while the serving runtime is blocking on KV warmup. This is different from simple proxy buffering issues seen previously and explains why failures cluster when cold cache and header rotation coincide.

root_cause: API gateway's handling of mid-stream HTTP/2 HEADERS frames interacts poorly with ALB idle timeout and serving runtime KV-cache warmup, causing target connections to be torn down during long prefix loads when clients rotate tracing headers mid-stream.
resolution:
Workaround applied: increased ALB idle timeout to 120s for affected customer target groups and asked customer to temporarily stop rotating trace headers. We also added a mitigation flag in APIGW to avoid re-encoding headers mid-stream for long-lived streaming requests.
Permanent fix: runtime+gateway engineering will implement a change to tolerate mid-stream header updates by treating them as metadata-only (no upstream re-encode), and add a heuristic to detect in-progress KV-cache warmups and extend idle timers. Planned rollout: canary next week, full rollout in 2 weeks.
Follow-ups: add console alerting for 'streaming header-change disconnects', update public runbook, and review default ALB idle timeout recommendation in our docs.
